messages.author: 3648aa30fc058f11
messages.subject: calibration errors circles
parts:
Hi Chris,

I'm trying to calibrate some datasets following the "Telemetry error vignette"  aiming to avoid  simultaneous calibration process when variogram.fit function will be applied.  But, something seems to be wrong (or not). Please, take a look at the plot (with 95% error discs) attached and let me know what do you think(calibrated_with_error_inf.png)?  This dataset has ambiguous DOP information and Fix-type (3D-V Fix, 3D Fix and 2D Fix). I converted Fix-type values to "3" for 3D-V Fix / 3D Fix and "2" for 2D Fix, just to make things more simple. Both variables are imported into a telemetry object.
Below,  the output of UERE summary:

, , horizontal
       low      est     high
2  959.307 1167.895 1376.082
3 1271.771 1285.304 1298.835
, , vertical
       low      est     high
2 5.337583 7.134605 8.928168
3 9.641533 9.787270 9.932978

The second plot (calibrated_no_error_inf.png) was made for a test purposes and brought me a similar behaviour. In this dataset I ripped out the calibration data, DOP and Fix-type variables.
Below,  UERE results from the dataset without errors information.
, , horizontal
        low      est     high
all 2820.98 2850.946 2880.907
, , vertical
         low      est     high
all 22.45758 22.79644 23.13524

For calibration data I have a sample with 3 days of irregular schedule (something about 30 fixes) because the GPS was left on the ground inside the wood to simulate errors as you recommend in the "...handling errors..." manuscript . You believe this little sample will be enough for calibrations I have to do?

If I run a calibration process without a second dataset for reference should I have any acceptable  results? Some datasets I have keeps thousands of relocations and I wondering if It could be enough for calibration process?

I don't remember where I read before, but It is worth remove Fix-type errors values if we have a DOP error information available? Even with ambiguous DOP ?


Thanks for while,

Sergio.

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: calibration errors circles
parts:
Hi Sergio,

If you are worried about the certainty of the calibration, then you can do some sensitivity analysis to see how the results are influenced with different calibration statistics. In a future update, I'm going to have small amounts of calibration data act as a sort of prior, so that the uncertainty will be included automatically.

More importantly, though, are you sure that is calibration data? The location estimates are kilometers apart? If the collar/tag was moved, then you need to break up the data.

As for fix-type, you only need it if the DOP values are on different scales, which can happen when the locations are estimated differently (e.g. Telonics). You can test if this is important with model selection.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 3648aa30fc058f11
messages.subject: Re: calibration errors circles
parts:
Hi Chris,

It is great heard  that some calibration data will be included in the future for comparison and references. I will navigate deeply in a sensitivity analysis to try find my certainty.

About your question: "...are you sure that is calibration data?" Yes, I am sure about the calibration data is present in the animal dataset. To build the calibration dataset I picked up a few amount of data when I had sure those fixes came from a period when the collar was resting on the ground, which is the moment after collar have been dropped-off the animal neck and the time I took to retrieve collar back from the field. This situation occurred with other collars and now I am wondering, if I separate this moment, from each collar, I retrieve back and put it all data together in one dataset (to create a more detailed calibration dataset) could it be works well? These collars share the same information protocol, so there is no chance of incompatibility information problems between different data sources, except the fact each collar came from a different locations and different time moments (year/month).   

Your second question: "The location estimates are kilometers apart?" Yes, I suppose this information should be correct because the animal in question is a Puma. Sometimes, they sneak around exaggeratedly in one night only. But, perhaps I could be done something wrong when I decided put together, in the same dataset, the calibration data and animal data? That's is a point where I am still make some confusing yet. CTMM is a brand new tool for me and as newbie some mistakes from that order could be happening until I have 100% of sure about what I am doing with CTMM. 
 
I tested Fix-type and DOP variables together and separately and I didn't noticed any expressive difference between one and the other for model selection.

Thanks for help.

Best regards,

Sergio.

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: calibration errors circles
parts:
Hi Sergio,

You need to separate the different periods in the data where the collar was at different locations (and not moving), say with a different ID. The error circles should then be tens of meters instead of kilometers.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: calibration errors circles
parts:
Hi Sergio,

That warning is fine.

You need to have your tracking and calibration data imported into separate telemetry objects, but they can be in the same CSV file (with different IDs) and resulting list of telemetry objects, as with the turtle example in the vignette. Furthermore, the different calibration deployments need to be imported into separate telemetry objects as well (by using different IDs).

Best,
Chris
